ledger.claim: The deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. The trace measures 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km, an excess of 5.97 km or 33.17%, which passes both POL-RD-01 tests at once: greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km. No clause of POL-RD-01 saves the driver once that test is met.

POL-RD-01 fixes the governing measurement as gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 23.97 km, not the rounded 24.0 km convenience copy on the trip record. The excess to be worked is therefore 5.97 km, and trip_record.actual_distance_km may not be cited for the threshold test.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 241 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, max_gap_sec of 0.0 and no straight-line jump approaching 500 m. Limbs (a) to (c) are not engaged, so no independent corroboration is required and the deviation stands on the trace itself.

The fare is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 has no application and the rider is not confined to a pass-through-only remedy. The POL-RD-02 recomputation is the governing arithmetic for this trip.

Run the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on its separate lines: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 18.0 km = 13.50 + 0.28 x 30 min = 8.40) x 1.6 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 of on-optimal-route ERP = 44.42. Charged_total = 58.10. Refund = 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to SGD 13.70. That is 23.5% of the charge, far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

The recomputation preserves the 1.6 surge the rider has accepted, applying it to base, distance and time only and not to the 4.50 of ERP. That is why the refund of 13.68 tracks the excess distance alone rather than stripping out the surge the rider agreed to pay, and why the rider does not seek the full contested amount.

No traffic advisory exonerates this detour. EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING - it carries no payload, a weight_multiplier of 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - and no advisory in the pool names the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses; with none on file the clause cannot run, and the driver's 'AYE was crawling' assertion exonerates nothing.

POL-RD-04 is unavailable. The whole chat log is two messages: the rider asking 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' and the driver replying 'AYE jam boss, this way faster'. Neither is a rider instruction to take a named road; the rider's message is a query and the driver's is his own claim of congestion. Both messages carry waypoint_hint null, so there is no resolved waypoint to corroborate and nothing here transfers the cost of the detour to the rider.

POL-RD-05 cannot be run. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no amended endpoint and no re-quote against which a smaller excess could be measured. Nothing in the record reduces the 5.97 km excess or displaces the 18.0 km baseline.

POL-RD-12 does not bite. vehicle_type is RYDE_X and not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. The 18.0 km booked optimal is the correct baseline and no co-rider collection or set-down distance falls to be excluded from the excess.

The burden has shifted and the driver has not discharged it. Under POL-RD-08 the rider shows the artifacts describe the same trip - matching trip identifier and a consistent pickup and ride window across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown - and an excess over the POL-RD-01 threshold. The driver must then point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; he points to none. His counterparty statement and his chat reply name no advisory ID, and his own words ('I went up and over on the PIE. Longer on the map but it moved') concede the longer route without excusing it.

The rider is not a serial claimant and no extra corroboration is demanded of her. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, nowhere near the 4-or-more claims with 1-or-fewer substantiated that POL-RD-08 requires before imposing a corroboration requirement beyond the trace.

POL-RD-09(1) governs the ERP lines and the rider does not double-count them. The 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route and is properly included inside the recomputed fare; the 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route and is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, so it must NOT be added on top of the 13.70. The trace passes within 250 m of both gantries - nearest fixes at 0.0 m and 8.76 m - so neither line is a phantom charge under POL-RD-09(4).

POL-RD-01's establishment test is met and I do not contest it: the governing trace distance is 23.97 km against an 18.0 km booked optimal, an excess of 5.97 km — 33.17% — which clears both the 20% and the 0.8 km limbs. But the same clause's MATERIALITY limb is not met: 33.17% is below the 50% threshold and 5.97 km is below the 8.0 km threshold, so this is an established but NON-MATERIAL deviation. The consequences that attach only to a material deviation — the driver_profile check being required, the balance being resolved against the driver, the FULL_REFUND uplift and the driver-conduct referral — are therefore unavailable on this trip.

Even if POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is run, no repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the threshold of 3, and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 412 is 0.24%, below the 5% ratio limb — and the drivers' lifetime field prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-window counter this clause names, so it must not be substituted for it. No pattern means no resolution of the balance against the driver, no uplift of the POL-RD-02 figure to a FULL_REFUND, and no referral to driver-conduct review.

ledger.claim: The driver's account of a crawling AYE is an external-cause defence, and it is asserted with no traffic_advisory to stand on: the only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00114-01, is MISSING — admissibility weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING, no payload in the pool. I disclose that impairment, and the absence itself is citable. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses within a validity window, so no exoneration can be granted on this record, and the driver cannot discharge his shifted burden under POL-RD-08 by asserting traffic that names no advisory ID. Because the exculpatory clause is invoked against an artifact missing from the pool — the case POL-RD-10(5) gives as 'a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory' — the judge must ESCALATE rather than rule: no monetary outcome issues and the disputed amount is held while a human reviewer determines whether that corridor was congested in the 18:36-19:20 window on 7 August 2026.

If the case is decided on money rather than escalated, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic fixes the ceiling and it is well below the sum pleaded: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-optimal-route ERP = 44.42, against a charged_total of 58.10, leaving 13.68 rounded up to SGD 13.70. The SGD 2.00 Adam Road gantry is already comprehended in that figure through the recomputation — only the on-optimal-route Kim Keat Link gantry's SGD 2.50 is passed through — so under POL-RD-09(1) it can never be added on top of the refund as a second item.

The rider expressly accepts the 1.6x surge, and the recomputation preserves it: the same 1.6 multiplier recorded on the fare breakdown is applied to the optimal base, distance and time charges, so the SGD 13.70 on the POL-RD-02 computation reaches only the distance and time attributable to the 5.97 km of excess. The base fare, the platform fee and the surge — and the SGD 0.00 of refund already issued — are left standing; nothing in the rider's case is a challenge to, or a recovery of, the surge.

The claim as pleaded is overstated on its own numbers. The rider asks me to answer for 'the extra 6 km', but POL-RD-01 makes the trace distance the governing field and forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test: the excess is 5.97 km, not 6 km, against the 23.97 km the trace records. Consistently, the SGD 15.00 contested exceeds the SGD 13.70 that the POL-RD-02 arithmetic can produce on this record, so the pleading cannot set the quantum.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties:

The deviation is established, but it is not material. On the governing GPS trace the trip ran 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.17%. That passes both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (above 0.8 km and above 20%), so the finding rests on this trip's own evidence; I used the trace distance, not the rounded 24.0 km copy on the trip record, as POL-RD-01 requires. It does not reach materiality (above 50% or above 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged. Even if it were, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 (below 3) and 1 over 412 completed trips is 0.24% (below 5%), and the lifetime field prior_deviation_flags may not be substituted — so no pattern is established, and the FULL_REFUND uplift and the conduct referral that attach to a material deviation are unavailable. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d of 1 does not impose a corroboration requirement either.

No clause excuses the detour. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic advisory naming a corridor the optimal route uses, and there is none: no advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36–19:20 window. POL-RD-04: the two-message chat log is a rider query, not an instruction to take a named road, and both messages carry a null waypoint, so the corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable. POL-RD-05: no endpoint was amended. POL-RD-11: the fare is METERED with no quoted fare. POL-RD-12: the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL.

On the request to escalate under POL-RD-10(5): I decline. That trigger fires where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited artifact that is missing, does not cover the window, or lacks a field the clause needs. The driver's account ('AYE was crawling') names no artifact and cites no evidence, so it stands as a bare exculpatory assertion — discarded under POL-RD-08, the clause that places the burden on the driver — and it does not make the case undecidable. The record affirmatively shows that no advisory exists, so the case can be, and is, decided.

Money, on POL-RD-02: charged_total = 58.10. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 × 18.0 km = 13.50 + 0.28 × 30 min = 8.40) × 1.6 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-optimal-route ERP = (25.70 × 1.6) + 3.30 = 41.12 + 3.30 = 44.42. Refund = 58.10 − 44.42 = 13.68, rounded up to SGD 13.70. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

The 1.6 surge you accepted is preserved: it is applied to base, distance and time only, never to the ERP, so the refund tracks the excess distance alone. The 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route and is already inside the recomputed fare; the 2.00 Adam Road gantry is off-route and is comprehended in the refund under POL-RD-09(1), so it is not added on top of the 13.70. Both gantries are matched to the trace — nearest fixes at 0.0 m and 8.76 m — so there is no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4). The sum pleaded, 15.00, exceeds what the arithmetic can produce; the refund is the computed 13.70.

Confidence: the artifacts carrying the deciding facts — trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown — each carry weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0; I set confidence at 0.90.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
